stem:
Zara's school van has AMBULANCE lettering painted in reverse on the front so drivers ahead can read it in their rear-view mirrors. She faces a plane mirror, raises her right hand, and wears a badge with an upward-pointing arrow.

Which claims correctly apply lateral inversion? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: In the plane mirror, her raised right hand appears as a raised left hand.
The reversed AMBULANCE lettering reads as AMBULANCE in a rear-view mirror.
The upward-pointing arrow on her badge points downward in the plane mirror.
Ordinary forward AMBULANCE lettering reads normally as AMBULANCE in the rear-view mirror.

teacher.key_rationale: Lateral inversion swaps left and right, so a raised right hand looks like a raised left hand, and reversed AMBULANCE lettering reads correctly in a mirror. Up-down is not swapped that way, and ordinary forward lettering does not read normally in the rear-view mirror.
